episode_summary: Hashing It Out interview with Jordi Baylina of Polygon on his path from the Catalan independence movement and Giveth/DAppNode into ZK tooling (Circom, SnarkJS, Hermes), and on recursion, STARK vs SNARK proving, zkEVM performance goals and how Polygon organises its engineering team.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said he was one of the white hat researchers who worked on The DAO.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: I was one of the white hats in the DAO.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said he wrote Circom and SnarkJS as learning tools that the industry now widely uses.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: For me, I wrote Circom and Snark.js.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Hermes was a payment-only ZK rollup that his team built before joining Polygon.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: Hermes is a payment roll-ups, payment-only roll-ups.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said he funded Giveth with Griff Green at the beginning and also funded DAppNode.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: I funded Gibbeth with Griff at the beginning. I funded Dapnode.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said that when he tried to use blockchains for the Catalan independence movement around 2016 and 2017, nothing worked in practice.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: nothing works that is from the practical sense.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Spain's government had web pages censored by the main ISPs in about two minutes during the Catalan independence fight.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: And it took like two minutes to just call to the main ISPs and just told them you have to censor this page, this page, and this page.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Catalan users of IPFS were mainly going through a centralized gateway, which was censored.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: the people that were using ipfs were mainly using the gateway with the gateway is very centralized so actually they censor the gateway

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said the Catalan government put a page telling citizens where to vote, and that page was censored.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: They wanted to vote, and the Catalan government just put a web page saying where they had to go to vote.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina used a medical insurance example to explain that zero-knowledge proofs let someone prove a yes or no without revealing their whole history.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: With zero knowledge, you can prove a yes, you can prove a no.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said a ZK proof can be verified in a few milliseconds no matter how long the program that produced it ran.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: And this verification, it takes a few milliseconds,

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said privacy and compression can both be achieved in ZK rollups, but not in the same proof, using recursion.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: Yes, it's absolutely possible, but it cannot be done in the same proof.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Polygon was using proof aggregation extensively, producing trees of proofs.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: In Polygon, we are using extensively the aggregation.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said recursion is very straightforward in STARKs, unlike elliptic-curve based SNARKs.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: The Starks does not have this constraint. So doing recursion in a Stark is very straightforward.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Polygon verifies a STARK inside a STARK just before posting the final proof on-chain, to make it smaller.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: And in the last minute, just before sending the proof on chain, in order to be smaller, we verify a stark with a stark.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said STARKs are at least one order of magnitude faster overall than elliptic-curve based systems.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: so starts are one order of magnitude, at least one order of magnitude faster

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said the current Polygon zkEVM proof is very much optimized for cost rather than latency.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: In the case of the CKVM, the current proof is very much optimized for cost.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said people working in ZK may need to spend around 50% of their time keeping up with research.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: But if you are in this space, spending 50% of your time keeping up and understanding what's going on and so on is not a crazy number.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Polygon Hermes had fewer than 20 engineers at the time.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: Polygon Hermes, right now we are less than 20 engineers.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said he would be happy when the Polygon zkEVM network was 100 times more capacity and faster than Ethereum.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: i will be happy when at least the the network is 100 times more capacity and faster than Ethereum.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said Ethereum's EIP-4844 and danksharding were important pieces that needed to happen for the zkEVM goal.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: Here, EAP4844 and tank sharding are important pieces that need to happen

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina said he expected ZK rollup systems to speed up a lot in the coming months and years.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: and I expect that the systems will speed up a lot in the next month, years, if you want, but I mean very, very fast.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina argued that any published risk figure that is hard to grasp should come with an analogy so people understand it.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: then you need to have an analogy associated with it so people get it.

cards.claim: Jordi Baylina defined zero knowledge in one line as a proof of a program without having to compute it.
cards.speaker: Jordi Baylina
cards.quote: It's just proof of program without having to compute it.

cards.claim: The host said Jordi Baylina and Griff Green started Giveth and wrote the MiniMe token contract, a flavour of ERC20 with snapshots.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the mini me token contract which is a like a flavor of urc20

cards.claim: The host said white hat hackers stay ethical largely because crypto's ideals appeal to them and the community rewards disclosure.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's because the ideals of what crypto is trying to do appeal to them.

title: Jordi Baylina of Polygon zkEVM | Zero Knowledge, Privacy, Scalability and Building Useful Technology
